Chhattisgarh ---- Respondents (Cause-title taken from Case Information System) For Petitioners : Mr. Siddharth Shukla, Advocate For State : Ms. Abhiyunati Singh, Panel Lawyer Hon'ble Shri Justice Rakesh Mohan Pandey Order on Board 17.08.2023 Heard.

1) The petitioners have challenged the FIR, charge-sheet and the criminal case registered in connection with Crime No.07/2021 dated 30.01.2021 at Police Station- Mahila Thana, Ambikapur, District- Surguja (C.G.) against them for commission of offence punishable under Section 498-A read with Section 34 of the IPC.

2) The facts of the present case are that the marriage between petitioner No.3 and respondent No.2 was solemnized on 29.11.2014 and after two years and 8 months, the respondent No.2/wife left her matrimonial house making allegation that she was subjected to cruelty and harassment.
There are specific allegations regarding physical as well as mental cruelty along with demand of dowry against the petitioners.

It is further stated that on 24.07.2017 when these facts were narrated to father of respondent No.2, she was taken back at Ambikapur and in the year 2019, she was allured to enter into compromise and her jewellery were taken back by the present petitioners, because of that, she Harvinder Singh Vasier vs State Of Chhattisgarh on 17 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/199499033/
1 was in depression, therefore on 30.01.2021, she made a complaint.
3) Learned counsel for the petitioners would submit that undisputedly the respondent No.2 left her matrimonal house on 24.07.2017, whereas, report was lodged on 30.01.2021 and thus, the same is barred by limitation according to provisions of Section 468 of the Cr.P.C.

sentences.text: He would further submit that the matter was settled between the parties on 15.07.2019 and it was agreed between the parties to not implicate each other in any litigation and to renegotiate the terms and conditions of the agreement.

He has placed reliance on the judgment passed by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the matter of Kamlesh Kalra Vs. Shilpika Kalra and others passed in Criminal Appeal No.416 of 2020 decided on 24th of April, 2020.

sentences.text: He would pray to quash the FIR, charge-sheet and criminal case pending against the petitioners.
4) On the other hand, learned counsel for the State would submit that respondent No.2 left her matrimonial house on 24.07.2017 and the same is evident from written report lodged by respondent No.2.

She would further submit that in the year 2019, she was called to enter into an agreement and it was so executed between the parties on 15.07.2019 but it is categorically stated in the written complaint that the petitioners grabbed her jewellery on pretext of a false agreement and it has given a new cause of action to the respondent No.2 to lodge FIR against the petitioners.
She would lastly submit that the present petition preferred by the petitioners deserves to be dismissed.
5) I have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the documents.
6) In the matter of Kamlesh Kalra (supra), the Hon'ble Supreme Court has affirmed the finding recorded by the High Court.

Para 12 & 13 reads as under :
"12.

After considering the decisions of this Court rendered in Vanka Radhamanohari vs Vanka Venkata Reddy (1993) 3 SCC 4 and Arun Vyas vs Anita Vyas (1999) 4 SCC 690, and the decisions of the High Court of Delhi in Asha Ahuja vs Rajesh Ahuja 2003 (68) DRJ 437 and S. K. Bhalla vs State of NCT of Delhi 2010 SCC OnLine Del 4384, the High Court held as under:
"..............
11.

sentences.text: As noted above, the allegations of the complainant are of harassment by the petitioners No.1 and 2 i.e. the husband and the mother-in-law.

Admittedly the respondent No.2 and petitioner No.1 are living separately since June 10, 2009 and there is no material to show that due to reconciliatory measures or for what reason the respondent No.2 failed to file the complaint on which the afore-noted FIR was registered till 28th January, 2013, i.e. beyond the period of limitation of three years.

Thus there being no justification for the delay in filing the complaint beyond the period of limitation and there being no allegation that the physical and mental harassment continued against respondent No.2 beyond June 10, 2009, petitioners No.1 and 2 are not liable to be proceeded under Section 498A IPC.

However, as noted above, Section 406 IPC is a continuing offence and every day of non-return of the Harvinder Singh Vasier vs State Of Chhattisgarh on 17 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/199499033/
2 istridhan articles would give fresh cause of action.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Admittedly, after the registration of the FIR petitioner No.1 sought to return certain istridhan articles thereby fortifying the claim of breach of trust.

However, one of the necessary ingredients for offence punishable under Section 406 IPC is entrustment and the complainant alleges entrustment of istridhan articles to petitioner No.2 and not petitioner No.1.
12.

Thus, this Court finds no ground to quash the FIR in question against petitioner No.2 for offence punishable under Section 406 IPC or the proceedings thereto."
13.
As regards, the finding recorded by the High Court in respect of complaint/FIR filed under Section 498A IPC, we are of the firm opinion that the same does not call for interference.

In the facts of this case, it is clear that the FIR filed in this regard in 2015 was time barred, having been filed much more than three years after the separation of Manish Kalra (husband) and Shilpika Kalra (wife) and the filing of the divorce petition by the husband, both in 2009.

In the facts of the case, the reasons given by the High Court for quashing the proceedings under section 498A IPC are justified and do not call for interference by this Court."
7) It is well settled principle of law that the offence punishable under Section 498-A of the IPC gives a recurring cause of action.
On 24.07.2017, respondent No.2 left her matrimonial house and thereafter, she was staying along with her parents.
She was called by the petitioners to enter into an agreement.
The parties entered into an agreement on 15.07.2019 and it is specific allegation of respondent No.2 that the petitioners grabbed her jewellery.

As the incident of 15.07.2019 has given a new cause of action in favour of respondent No.2, therefore, the complaint made by respondent No.2 was within limitation according to provisions of Section 468 of the Cr.P.C..
Therefore, the facts of the judgment relied on by learned counsel for the petitioners are distinguishable from the facts of the present case.

Learned counsel for the petitioners has further stated that an agreement was entered into between the parties and the dispute between them was settled and to renegotiate the terms and conditions of the agreement, respondent No.2 has lodged the FIR against the petitioners.

The contention made by learned counsel for the petitioners is not acceptable as there is allegation that the petitioners grabbed the jewellery of respondent No.2/complainant when she was called to enter into an agreement.
8) Taking into consideration the facts of the present case, I do not find any good ground to entertain the present petition.
Consequently, the petition fails and is hereby dismissed.
